requirements.title: A component part contains zero or more component definition statements
requirements.source: 7.5.4.1 R735; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 93, printed 79, line 3.
requirements.definition: The component part permits an empty sequence or repeated component definition statements. R726 determines its position, R736 selects the statement categories, and special type constraints can require components despite this optional grammar.

pending.empty-part-link: The current reviewed base includes R726_valid__empty in tests/fixtures/derived_definition_r726_valid__empty/fixture.json. The existing evidence-link schema cannot express this numbered wrapper/positive-only reuse. Keep the exact source/ID/fingerprint relation pending for coordinator integration; do not duplicate the empty definition.

requirements.oracle: An initialized run checks two independently declared INTEGER members. The empty component-part canonical link remains pending; no duplicate empty-type execution is added.
requirements.oracle_limitation: C745 restricts SEQUENCE and C1801-C1806 restrict BIND(C) definitions. An empty component part is not a universal permission for every type class. The prior definition implementation is outside this authoring scope.

requirements.title: Component definitions have data and procedure-pointer alternatives
requirements.definition: A component definition is a data-component definition or a procedure-component definition. Procedure-pointer components are not the type-bound-procedure part. Constraints attached to this union, including C759, apply in either alternative.

pending.data-alternative-link: Pending finite linkage to the planned R737_valid__plain control. Verify its actual R737 parse and local source point; do not execute a second identical case under R736.
pending.procedure-alternative-link: Pending finite linkage to the planned R741_valid__explicit_interface control. Verify a procedure-pointer component before any type CONTAINS, not a binding after CONTAINS. Keep the corresponding C759 nested type-parameter context in the use graph.

requirements.oracle: Source plan only. Two canonical alternative edges will retain their defining grammar and execution owners.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A syntax union supplies no blanket permission for every nested declaration-type-spec, initialization or attribute. A parser accepting PROCEDURE somewhere does not establish the component alternative.

requirements.title: A data component statement has a type, optional attribute separator and declarator list
requirements.definition: A declaration-type-spec precedes a nonempty component-decl list. A double colon may occur without attributes; if component attributes occur, their comma-led list is followed by the double colon. Initializers independently require that separator under C766. The component context still restricts alternatives of the canonical declaration-type-spec.

pending.type-specifier-use-graph: Pending finite graph over R703's ten declaration-type alternatives. Map intrinsic/TYPE(intrinsic), prior derived/enum/enumeration, CLASS with extensibility and POINTER/ALLOCATABLE, CLASS(*), forbidden component TYPE(*) via C714, and prior-data-ref TYPEOF/CLASSOF via C709-C712. C709_valid__components is existing canonical context, not new R737 credit. Preserve all canonical restrictions and independently review any proposed link.

requirements.oracle: Two initialized runs distinguish bare and double-colon two-member declarations. A compile pair inserts only the missing :: after POINTER, retaining the correct deferred shape. The full declaration-type-spec descendant graph remains pending.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A bare expected/type/attribute message is insufficient, even at the declaration line. F2023 TYPEOF/CLASSOF or named enum feature failures cannot corroborate a syntax restriction. C766 is not re-owned here.

requirements.title: Data component attributes use six specified syntactic alternatives
requirements.definition: Component attributes comprise an access-spec, ALLOCATABLE, CODIMENSION with a bracketed coarray-spec, CONTIGUOUS, DIMENSION with a component-array-spec, or POINTER. The CODIMENSION payload is enclosed in square brackets, not parentheses. PUBLIC and PRIVATE are the two access-spec spellings. Membership does not waive C748-C757 or canonical scope, shape, association and accessibility rules.

pending.codimension: Pending admission/link plan for INTEGER, ALLOCATABLE, CODIMENSION[:,:] :: field, followed by the allocated-corank run under S7.5.4.3-001. Type-only admission does not supply a runtime corank observation. Keep C751, C822, C825-C827 and the saved containing-object premise.
pending.dimension: Pending finite linkage to S7.5.4.2-001's shared DIMENSION(2,3) initialized run; use R740's component-array-spec, not the broader R814 array grammar. Do not duplicate that execution.

requirements.oracle: Module/consumer runs exercise PUBLIC and PRIVATE data components without invalid private-name references. Separate runs establish allocation, scalar pointer association and CONTIGUOUS array-pointer association before inquiries and typed mutation. Shared DIMENSION and CODIMENSION reuse facets remain pending.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No C ABI, byte width, storage contiguity of arrays of structures, or processor kind-number convention is assumed. Contiguity of an appropriate whole TARGET array is a language premise, not a physical-layout inference.

requirements.title: Individual data component declarators can specify shape, coshape, length and initialization
requirements.definition: Each declarator has a component name, followed in order by an optional parenthesized component-array-spec, optional bracketed coarray-spec, optional * char-length, and optional component-initialization. These suffixes belong to that named component, not automatically to every member of the statement. Their canonical constraints remain in force.

pending.named-list: Pending linkage to R737_valid__plain and S7.5.4.1-001's two-member statement. Verify each declarator is independently named and receives only its own suffixes; do not create a second list-admission execution.
pending.individual-array-link: Pending finite source link to S7.5.4.2-001's local shape and individual override runs; record the exact suffix and statement-level DIMENSION separately.
pending.individual-coarray-link: Pending finite source link to S7.5.4.3-001's local deferred coshape and individual corank override runs. Confirm both arrayspec-then-coarrayspec ordering and ALLOCATABLE.
pending.individual-character-link: Pending link to existing S7_4_4_2_004_valid__component at tests/clause07/S7_4_4_2_004_valid__component.f90. It retains individual lengths two/zero and a shared length five with actual values. Review the exact execution fingerprint and semantic link; no metadata change or duplicate execution now.
pending.initialization-use-graph: Pending four finite declaration contexts: nonpointer = constant, data pointer => NULL(), data pointer => a constant-designated SAVE TARGET, and allocatable without an explicit initializer. Map R743/C766-C770 and 7.5.4.6's initialization/override rules, including inherited/direct components, constant parameter/bound restrictions and no implied SAVE for the enclosing object. The procedure-pointer initializer route has separate R1515/R1517 ownership. No initialization catalogue is claimed here.

requirements.oracle: Source plan only. Declarator syntax and suffix locality are linked to their actual canonical controls/effects. Default initialization is not inferred from successful declaration parsing.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The optional grammar alone does not permit initialization of allocatables, arbitrary initial pointer targets, or nonconstant default-initialized component bounds. Existing character source bytes and case IDs remain unchanged.

requirements.title: Component array syntax selects explicit-shape or deferred-shape lists
requirements.definition: The component-array-spec alternatives are an explicit-shape-spec-list and a deferred-shape-spec-list. They are narrower than the general array-spec union; C750 and C754 select the required alternative according to POINTER/ALLOCATABLE. Each explicit bound also has C755's component-specific expression context.

pending.explicit-shape-link: Pending link to the planned C754 explicit-shape controls and S7.5.4.2-001's defined rank/bound runs. Confirm the actual scalar-bound list, not just an array-valued query result.
pending.deferred-shape-link: Pending link to the planned C750 POINTER and ALLOCATABLE controls using (:) and (:,:). Their fixed rank comes from the colon count; bounds are not queried before association/allocation.
pending.general-array-grammar-exclusion-graph: Pending finite grammar graph for four general-array forms: assumed-shape (0:), assumed-size (*), assumed-rank (..), and the F2023 vector-bound form ([2,3]). Map why none is an additional R740 alternative; (:), although shared spelling, is deferred shape in the relevant component context. Before any negative, select one primary owner and a repair to (2) or (2,3), prove every remaining C750/C754 premise, and require a component-shape cause rather than unsupported-general-array recovery.

requirements.oracle: Source plan only. Actual component shapes and canonical scalar-expression constraints remain separately traceable; a union is not multiplied into duplicate executions.
requirements.oracle_limitation: R814's newer general array forms do not automatically extend R740. A rank/type complaint about a vector bound can be an inherited scalar-expression restriction, not proof of another shape facet.

requirements.title: A data component statement does not repeat a component attribute
requirements.definition: A component-attr-spec does not recur in a single component definition statement. The subject is a data component attribute list, not a TYPE header, a procedure component list or a type-bound binding.
requirements.oracle: Seven compile diagnostic/control pairs isolate repeated PUBLIC, PRIVATE, ALLOCATABLE, CODIMENSION, CONTIGUOUS, DIMENSION and POINTER. Each control deletes one duplicate while preserving independently legal module, shape, coshape and array-pointer premises. Causes identify the actual data component and attribute.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Broad duplicate/attribute/type strings cannot identify the subject. Repeated TYPE attributes belong to C735, procedure component attributes to C760, and binding attributes to C783. Same-line wrong-role reports and unsupported facilities remain failures.

requirements.title: An ordinary data component uses an intrinsic or previously defined nonintrinsic type
requirements.definition: When neither POINTER nor ALLOCATABLE occurs, the component's declaration-type-spec identifies an intrinsic type or a derived, enum or enumeration type already defined. The prior-definition qualification applies to those nonintrinsic alternatives. The conditional restriction does not itself forbid recursive or later-defined derived types behind permitted indirection. It does not waive C7112/C7116, which independently require prior enum/enumeration definitions, or other declaration requirements.
requirements.oracle: Initialized intrinsic and previously defined derived member runs accompany type-only named enum/enumeration admissions. Self/forward nonindirect components have exact repaired controls. The self POINTER repair also supplies that real indirection boundary; a separate ALLOCATABLE repair and two forward-indirection admissions complete the four finite boundary contexts without duplicate self-pointer execution.
requirements.oracle_limitation: CLASS(*) and TYPE(*) do not become ordinary by-value data component types merely because they occur in R703; C708/C714 remain applicable. Forward-use allowances are not a permission to leave a type undefined. No matching storage layout proves type identity.

requirements.title: Pointer and allocatable component arrays have deferred shape
requirements.definition: If POINTER or ALLOCATABLE is specified, every component-array-spec is a deferred-shape list. This applies to the DIMENSION attribute and individual component suffixes. It does not require a scalar component to acquire array shape.
requirements.oracle: Five compile pairs change only the actual explicit component shape to a deferred shape, separately for POINTER/ALLOCATABLE and local/shared specifications. The overridden DIMENSION pair keeps an already-deferred local suffix and changes only the invalid shared specification. Scalars are not made missing-shape negatives.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Messages about missing ALLOCATABLE, illegal POINTER/ALLOCATABLE coexistence or an unsupported deferred-array facility cannot count as the required shape cause. Sizes/bounds of unallocated or unassociated arrays are not expected values.

requirements.title: A coarray component has deferred coshape and ALLOCATABLE
requirements.definition: A coarray-spec in a data component statement requires a deferred-coshape list and the ALLOCATABLE attribute. Both the CODIMENSION attribute and an individual coarray suffix are covered. Corank, array rank and runtime cobounds remain different properties.
requirements.oracle: Five coarray type-only pairs separate explicit-versus-deferred coshape, missing ALLOCATABLE and invalid overridden shared coshape. Controls change only that list or attribute. No containing object, allocation or private intrinsic-module value is needed for these declaration diagnostics.
requirements.oracle_limitation: C827 and C828 have overlapping general coarray-shape conditions. A report must express the actual cause for the selected component, not be credited merely for a coarray noun. Unsupported facilities, ASR failures and resource failures stay failures.

requirements.title: Coarray components exclude three particular intrinsic-module types
requirements.definition: A component with a coarray-spec cannot have the ISO_C_BINDING type C_PTR or C_FUNPTR, or the ISO_FORTRAN_ENV type TEAM_TYPE. These are module-provided type identities, not a ban on coincidentally spelled unrelated type names, integer kind values or every derived type.
requirements.oracle: Six type-only pairs use the actual C_PTR, C_FUNPTR or TEAM_TYPE identity through original and renamed imports. Replacing only the component type with INTEGER retains ALLOCATABLE and deferred coshape. One separate admission defines unrelated local types with those spellings, without inspecting opaque values or claiming C ABI compatibility.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The general exclusion C824 is a canonical dependency. C_PTR/C_FUNPTR/TEAM_TYPE presence does not establish representation or companion pairing, and unsupported module/type facilities cannot corroborate this restriction.
requirements.dependencies: C751/C749 (PDF 93); C824 and R809 (PDF 121); ISO_C_BINDING 18.2.1-.2 (PDF 516); TEAM_TYPE 16.10.2.34 (PDF 477); use association and type identity retain their canonical owners; 4.2 p2(3) (PDF 46).

requirements.title: A component with coarray potential subobjects is an ordinary scalar
requirements.definition: If the type of a data component has a coarray potential subobject component, that data component is scalar, lacks both POINTER and ALLOCATABLE, and is not itself a coarray. Potential-subobject traversal follows nonpointer derived components, including the canonical inherited-component paths; it is not a byte-layout or direct-member-only test.

pending.not-coarray-interaction: Pending finite two-node constraint graph: C751 makes a coarray component ALLOCATABLE, while C753 requires both nonallocatable and noncoarray. A prospective TYPE(leaf), ALLOCATABLE :: field[:] negative necessarily violates both C753 consequents; replacing TYPE(leaf) with INTEGER is a one-span valid repair. Do not present it as an isolated no-coarray-only experiment or credit it to an unrelated C751 failure.
pending.nested-and-inherited-use-graph: Pending finite graph with a direct leaf coarray, one ordinary scalar wrapper, and one inherited coarray component. Check 7.5.1 p5 and 7.5.7.2/C741-C742 at every edge before selecting any declaration pairs. A POINTER or ALLOCATABLE wrapper cannot hide a forbidden coarray-potential type: C753/C825 can already make that purported control invalid. No invalid intermediate type is permitted as an earlier masking error.

requirements.oracle: Three type-only pairs retain the complete leaf with its legal allocatable coarray and remove only the outer component's POINTER, ALLOCATABLE or array shape. Source relations distinguish the outer field from the leaf coarray. The coupled nonallocatable/noncoarray consequence and nested/inherited use graphs remain pending.
requirements.oracle_limitation: These declarations do not establish valid containing-object contexts automatically; C825/C826 still govern variables, pointers, coarrays and SAVE/ALLOCATABLE/dummy/associate contexts. The compound coarray branch remains pending graph work, not a claimed single-cause fixture.

requirements.title: Nonpointer nonallocatable component arrays have explicit shape
requirements.definition: When a component statement has neither POINTER nor ALLOCATABLE, every component-array-spec is an explicit-shape list. This selects the ordinary array alternative without requiring an array specification on scalar components.
requirements.oracle: Three compile pairs repair the local or shared shape of an ordinary component, including a deferred shared DIMENSION overridden by an already-valid local explicit shape. The diagnostic must identify the actually invalid specification, not pretend the active local shape is invalid.
requirements.oracle_limitation: An ordinary scalar is not a missing-shape negative. Generic deferred-shape or expected-token text cannot substitute for the specific ordinary-component context.

requirements.title: Each explicit component bound is a component specification expression
requirements.definition: Every lower and upper bound in an explicit component shape satisfies the component specification expression definition in 10.1.11 p9, including its inherited scalar-integer and restricted-expression premises. That context excludes specification functions; ALLOCATED, ASSOCIATED, COMMAND_ARGUMENT_COUNT, EXTENDS_TYPE_OF, GET_TEAM, NUM_IMAGES, PRESENT, SAME_TYPE_AS, TEAM_NUMBER and THIS_IMAGE; nonconstant specification inquiries; and dependence on a variable value. TRANSFER has the additional constant-argument and disassociated-ultimate-pointer conditions. A type parameter is not an object: permitted own or inherited type parameters are not excluded merely because a LEN value is not a constant expression.

pending.forbidden-reference-use-graph: Pending finite graph enumerating all ten excluded intrinsic names in 10.1.11 p9. Distinguish the integer-returning cases from logical inquiries requiring a type-correct integer-valued wrapper. GET_TEAM returns TEAM_TYPE and must not be forced through an invalid numeric coercion or a second banned function and then called an isolated cause. Establish each function's argument/state premises and one minimal integer-expression repair before proposing a diagnostic case; otherwise retain that edge as documentary/source-only work.
pending.transfer-qualification-graph: Pending finite graph for a pointer-free constant-argument TRANSFER, a constant source with disassociated ultimate pointers, and violations of each of those two premises. Read the corresponding 10.1.12/TRANSFER interpretation before choosing a consumer. No guessed transferred value, descriptor bits, arithmetic/model query or arbitrary resulting array size is an oracle; this is not a real-BOZ representation workaround.

requirements.oracle: Three runs exercise abstract KIND/LEN parameter bounds, an inherited LEN bound and a constant property inquiry without reading the prototype's value. Four compile pairs replace a host-variable lower/upper bound, a valid specification-function call or an assumed-shape inquiry with a small literal. The actual component-bound dependency is the cause; the ten-intrinsic and TRANSFER graphs remain pending.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A blanket 'components must be constant' oracle would wrongly reject valid LEN-parameter bounds. Mere type/kind/constant/expected words and same-line placement cannot establish the cause. If a proposed expression violates another function argument or state precondition, its failure cannot be repurposed as C755 evidence.
requirements.dependencies: R403/C401 (PDF 45); 7.5.3.1 p5 and inherited parameters (PDF 92, 104); R815-R817 (PDF 125); 10.1.11 p1-p9, including the p9 continuation, and 10.1.12 p1 (PDF 185-188); C767 (PDF 96); 4.2 p2(3) (PDF 46).

requirements.title: A component is not both ALLOCATABLE and POINTER
requirements.definition: ALLOCATABLE and POINTER cannot both describe a component. Either attribute alone remains possible subject to its own shape, type and state restrictions.
requirements.oracle: Two negatives put POINTER and ALLOCATABLE on the same scalar or deferred-shape array component. Each has two independently minimal controls, deleting one attribute or the other. No pointer/allocation status is queried by these compile-only pairs.
requirements.oracle_limitation: C854 has a corresponding general POINTER restriction. The shared semantic relationship is not another execution or proof of allocation/pointer lifetime behavior.

requirements.title: A CONTIGUOUS component is an array pointer
requirements.definition: Specifying CONTIGUOUS on a component requires both array rank and POINTER. This is a declaration condition, separate from the later requirement that an associated target be contiguous.

pending.array-pointer-admission-link: Pending source link to R738_valid__contiguous after its live, defined whole TARGET and pointer association premises have been reviewed. C757 is not a separate physical-layout observation.

requirements.oracle: Two declaration pairs independently violate the array and POINTER predicates of CONTIGUOUS. Each minimal repair removes CONTIGUOUS, preserving the existing valid scalar-pointer or ordinary explicit-array category. The array-pointer positive-only reuse link remains pending.
requirements.oracle_limitation: C830's ordinary assumed-shape/assumed-rank alternatives do not make nonpointer components legal here. Unsupported CONTIGUOUS or generic attribute reports are insufficient. Contiguity of arrays of structures can be processor dependent and is not inferred.

requirements.title: An individual star-length suffix is only for character components
requirements.definition: The individual * char-length suffix in a component declarator is permitted only for a character component. It is not a kind/byte-size suffix for other component types.

pending.character-suffix-admission-link: Pending link to S7_4_4_2_004_valid__component, whose actual character suffixes and lengths already have a canonical owner. Preserve all bytes/IDs and do not add a duplicate run.

requirements.oracle: Two compile pairs remove only the individual *2 suffix from INTEGER or previously defined derived components. Causes must concern the character-length suffix on that noncharacter field. Existing character-component admission retains its owner and remains a pending link.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A suffix's expression validity remains subject to C759 and character syntax; this type restriction does not permit assumed length or arbitrary processor storage notation. No assumed byte width is used.

requirements.title: Type-parameter values throughout component definitions are deferred or component specification expressions
requirements.definition: Each type-param-value within either kind of component definition is a colon or a component specification expression. The scope includes a typed proc-interface inside R741, not just data components. C702 still limits colon placement to POINTER/ALLOCATABLE entities and C701 still requires constant KIND values; local colon syntax is not a deferred-KIND permission. An asterisk is not one of C759's alternatives. Own or inherited type parameters can be valid expression primaries under the canonical rules.

pending.assumed-star-canonical-link: Pending link to C726_invalid:component in tests/clause07/C726_invalid.f90 and C726_valid__component_repair in its character_type fixture. Their primary owner, original isolation and sidecar contract remain untouched. Independently establish the C759 connection to that exact execution; never attach all six legacy C726 facets or executions to this component condition.
pending.expression-context-use-graph: Pending finite graph linking C759 to R701/C701/C702, 10.1.11 p9 and 10.1.12, and to the C755 expression-context matrix without duplicating its executions. Retain all ten excluded inquiry/function names, no specification functions, constant specification inquiries, no variable-value dependence and qualified TRANSFER. Audit one data LEN, one data KIND and one typed-procedure result LEN occurrence separately; bound diagnostics are not type-parameter diagnostics.

requirements.oracle: An own-LEN component run and two deferred data-length state/value runs retain the actual parameter contexts. Two data-selector pairs repair a host-variable length, including an overridden shared selector. The typed-procedure pair preserves fixed nonpolymorphic carrier objects and POINTER,NOPASS, replacing only MERGE(2,3,SAME_TYPE_AS(a,b)) with 2. That result is already constant; only the explicit component-expression inquiry exclusion is an intended cause. Canonical star and complete expression-context links remain pending.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No assumption that every component parameter is a constant, that every constant expression is a component specification expression, or that every colon is legal in every parameter slot. In particular an already-constant result expression must not receive credit from a false nonconstant-expression report. A result-type report for the wrong role, broad kind/constant/function text, missing-feature error, crash, verifier failure or unallocated-value query cannot corroborate this rule.
requirements.dependencies: R736/R741 (PDF 93-94); R701/C701/C702 (PDF 76); C726 and character lengths (PDF 84-85); 7.5.3.1 (PDF 91-92); 10.1.11 p3/p9 and 10.1.12 p1(6)/(7) (PDF 186-188); MERGE (PDF 433), SAME_TYPE_AS and extensible dynamic types (PDF 452, 79, 104); explicit-interface result requirements (PDF 325); R1513/15.4.3.6 p2-p4 (PDF 332-333); deferred parameter establishment (PDF 160-164, 195-196); 4.2 p2(3) (PDF 46).

requirements.title: A procedure component statement requires attributes and a double-colon declarator list
requirements.definition: PROCEDURE encloses an optional proc-interface in parentheses, then requires a comma, a nonempty procedure-component attribute list, a double colon and a nonempty proc-decl list. The canonical interface is an interface name or a declaration-type-spec; omission and a typed implicit function are distinct from a named explicit interface. C761 independently requires POINTER.

pending.initialization-use-graph: Pending finite canonical edges for a procedure component initialized by NULL() and by a compatible nonelemental module procedure. Map R1515/R1517/R1518/C1518/C1519 and 7.5.4.6 p3/p5, distinguishing component default initialization from standalone procedure-pointer initialization's SAVE implication. Independently prove matching interfaces and module-target lifetime before any run.

requirements.oracle: Explicit, omitted and typed implicit interfaces have real associated procedure-component invocations with compatible nonelemental targets. The implicit-interface calls are positional and avoid independently required explicit interfaces. A two-component list run uses distinct targets, and a compile pair inserts only the missing ::. Default initialization uses NULL() without arguments; its broader canonical-use graph stays pending.
requirements.oracle_limitation: R1513 is not redefined here, and its declaration-type-spec union is subject to C759 and all relevant function-result constraints. A nonexistent/unsupported interface is not a separator diagnostic. Undefined association status is never queried or invoked.

requirements.title: Procedure component attributes select access, passing mode and POINTER
requirements.definition: A procedure component attribute is an access-spec, NOPASS, PASS optionally naming a dummy argument, or POINTER. These are not the different binding-attr alternatives, and POINTER is mandatory for every such component under C761. Passing-mode semantics and passed-object characteristics have separate defining owners.

pending.nopass-link: Pending finite linkage to S7.5.4.5-001's component NOPASS run; its ordinary arguments remain explicit. R741's implicit-interface controls separately satisfy C762.
pending.bare-pass-link: Pending finite linkage to S7.5.4.5-002's component PASS run with first dummy self. All C765 characteristics are independently established.
pending.named-pass-link: Pending finite linkage to S7.5.4.5-003's second-position self component run. C763 owns name existence, C764 owns incompatibility with NOPASS.
pending.pointer-link: Pending linkage to C761's missing-POINTER pair and valid R741 controls. A procedure binding is not made a component simply because it names a procedure.

requirements.oracle: Two module/consumer runs admit public and private procedure components with association established by a module procedure. A public component is called directly; the private one only through an accessible wrapper. Passing-mode and POINTER canonical links remain pending rather than duplicating their executions.
requirements.oracle_limitation: DEFERRED and NON_OVERRIDABLE are binding attributes, not new R742 alternatives. Component-part and binding-part PRIVATE defaults are distinct; no source use graph may merge them.

requirements.title: A procedure component statement does not repeat a procedure component attribute
requirements.definition: The same procedure-component attribute cannot occur twice in one procedure component statement. Access attributes, POINTER and the same passing-mode attribute remain distinct subjects from data component or type-bound binding duplicates.
requirements.oracle: Six compile pairs delete one repeated PUBLIC, PRIVATE, POINTER, NOPASS, PASS or PASS(self) attribute from a procedure component. Explicit interfaces and the surviving POINTER/passing mode remain valid. Mixed PASS/NOPASS is not the duplicate-occurrence cause.
requirements.oracle_limitation: An exact source point does not disambiguate a duplicate on a component, binding, TYPE header or dummy. Generic attribute/type/function reports and missing-facility errors cannot substitute for the procedure-component duplicate.

requirements.title: Every procedure component attribute list includes POINTER
requirements.definition: POINTER is required in every procedure-component attribute list. A procedure component is not an ordinary external-procedure declaration or a type-bound procedure declaration.
requirements.oracle: One compile pair adds only POINTER to PROCEDURE(iface), NOPASS :: action with a complete explicit zero-argument interface and no initializer. The cause is this procedure component's missing POINTER, not an empty attribute list or an invocation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A message about a standalone procedure's EXTERNAL attribute, an initializer, or a binding is a different condition. Empty interface recovery does not count.

requirements.title: Implicit-interface and zero-argument procedure components require NOPASS
requirements.definition: A procedure-pointer component requires NOPASS if its interface is implicit or it has no arguments. These are alternative antecedents: a typed implicit interface is still implicit, while a named explicit interface can have an empty dummy list.

pending.explicit-passed-object-boundary: Pending link to S7.5.4.5-002's valid explicit interface with a scalar CLASS(record) first dummy and no NOPASS. A procedure with arguments is not automatically eligible: C765 must hold for its selected dummy.

requirements.oracle: Three compile pairs add only NOPASS, separately for an omitted interface, a typed implicit interface and an explicit zero-argument interface. Their cause sets do not cross-credit implicitness and absence of dummies. The explicit passed-object boundary reuse remains pending.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No fabricated invocation of a component with an undefined interface or association state is used. Broad function/argument/expected words do not establish either premise.
requirements.dependencies: R741 and 15.4.3.6 p2-p4 (PDF 94, 333); 7.5.4.5/C765 (PDF 96); explicit-interface requirements (PDF 324-325); 4.2 p2(3) (PDF 46).

requirements.title: The name in PASS identifies a dummy argument of the component interface
requirements.definition: PASS(arg-name) on a procedure component requires that exact Fortran dummy-argument name in its interface. It is a dummy name, not a component, procedure, result or positional label. Selection of the passed-object role is separately specified in 7.5.4.5.
requirements.oracle: One compile pair replaces PASS(absent) with PASS(self), retaining the explicit tag,self interface. A separate run uses case-equivalent PASS(sElF) on the real second dummy and verifies both hidden-object and ordinary argument values. A wrong-first-dummy recovery is not the missing-name cause.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A missing procedure or result name is not the missing dummy name. Same-line expected/function/type reports and wrong-first-dummy fallbacks are insufficient.

requirements.title: PASS and NOPASS do not coexist on a procedure component
requirements.definition: A single procedure-component attribute list cannot contain both PASS and NOPASS. PASS with or without a name is covered. This is distinct from repetition of the same attribute under C760.
requirements.oracle: Two negatives combine bare or named PASS with NOPASS. Each has two exact controls, removing one conflicting attribute while retaining POINTER and the valid explicit interface. No call is made with a NOPASS control's self argument accidentally omitted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: C786 is the separate binding-attribute owner. Do not accept a broad duplicate attribute or generic procedure report for a PASS/NOPASS conflict.

requirements.title: A data component statement distributes shared properties with individual overrides
requirements.definition: The statement's declaration-type-spec supplies the type and type parameters of every listed data component, with individual character-length suffixes able to set or override length. Its component attributes apply to the list, but an individual array specification sets or overrides DIMENSION and an individual coarray specification sets or overrides CODIMENSION. These exceptions are per component; rank, corank and character length are not interchangeable.
